evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Dengue is a re-emerging disease putting half the world at risk.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Dengue virus infects many people worldwide each year, making it a major global health concern.
allowed_evidence_spans: Dengue virus ( DENV ) is the most prevalent arbovirus leading to an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections every year .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: Dengue symptoms range from mild to potentially lethal forms.
evidence_rows.lay_context: People infected with dengue virus may experience mild symptoms or develop severe, dangerous forms of the disease.
allowed_evidence_spans: DENV can cause a spectrum of clinical manifestations , ranging from mild dengue fever ( DF ) to more life threatening forms such as dengue hemorrhagic fever ( DHF ) .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The mechanisms triggering the transition from mild dengue fever (DF) to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at the critical phase of infection are not well understood.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The mechanisms triggering the transition from mild dengue fever (DF) to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at the critical phase of infection are not well understood.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: The molecular reasons why dengue becomes severe are unclear.
evidence_rows.lay_context: It is not yet known why some patients develop severe dengue symptoms during the critical phase of illness.
allowed_evidence_spans: The clinical symptoms of DHF become evident typically at the critical phase of infection ( 5–7 days after onset of fever ) , yet the mechanisms that trigger transition from DF to DHF are not well understood .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: We know exactly how DF becomes DHF

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The study performed mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling was performed on sera from adult DF and DHF patients at critical and recovery phases.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: We analyzed blood samples to find molecular differences between mild and severe dengue.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Researchers used advanced techniques to measure small molecules in blood samples from dengue patients during key illness phases.
allowed_evidence_spans: We performed a mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of infection .

In the present study , metabolomics investigation was conducted on the same patient cohort at the critical phase ( day 5–7 post onset of fever ) and recovery phase ( day 21–28 post onset of fever ) to map the serum metabolome and identify metabolic pathways linked to dengue progression .

high_risk_check_facts.fact: Metabolomic profiling was performed on sera from adult DF and DHF patients at critical (day 5–7) and recovery (day 21–28) phases.
high_risk_check_facts.source_span: We performed a mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of infection .

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Twenty-nine metabolites were differentially expressed between DF and DHF patients at the critical phase, including bile acids, purines, acylcarnitines, phospholipids, and amino acids.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Twenty-nine metabolites differed between DF and DHF patients at the critical phase, including bile acids and other metabolite classes.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: We found many molecules that differ between mild and severe dengue.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Several types of small molecules in the blood showed different levels in patients with severe dengue compared to mild dengue during the critical illness phase.
allowed_evidence_spans: There were 29 differentially expressed metabolites identified between DF and DHF at the critical phase . These include bile acids , purines , acylcarnitines , phospholipids , and amino acids .
In the critical phase, a total of 29 MSI Levels 1 and 2 metabolites, were significantly expressed between DHF and DF patients, were identified.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: Bile acids were up to fivefold higher in DHF patients compared to DF patients at the critical phase and correlated with elevated liver enzymes AST and ALT, indicating liver injury in DHF.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Bile acids were up to 5 fold higher in DHF patients and correlated with higher AST and ALT levels, suggesting liver injury.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: High bile acid levels indicate liver damage in severe dengue.
evidence_rows.lay_context: Patients with severe dengue had much higher levels of bile acids in their blood, which were linked to signs of liver damage.
allowed_evidence_spans: Bile acids were observed up to 5 fold higher levels among DHF compared to DF patients and were significantly correlated to the higher levels of aspartate transaminase ( AST ) and alanine transaminase ( ALT ) , suggestive of liver injury among DHF .
Furthermore, these bile acids demonstrated positive correlations to AST and ALT levels, indicating they may be associated with liver dysfunction in DHF.

Put together , elevated bile acids among DHF patients and their positive correlations to AST and ALT levels indicated that these bile acids may play an important role in liver pathology in DHF patients .

In the clinic , liver enlargement and elevated transaminases have been used as the clinical features of hepatic histological changes in dengue patients [31] , and we indeed found in this study that AST and ALT levels were significantly higher in DHF than in DF .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: All dengue patients have liver injury

evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Altered metabolic pathways may serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate DHF.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: A Skp1-independent degradation pathway targets Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1, maintaining its degradation even under cadmium stress.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: Disruption of the Met30-Skp1 interaction, by cadmium stress or mutations, induces rapid degradation of Met30 via a Skp1-independent ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This pathway targets free F-box proteins and requires part of the SCF core.
evidence_rows.lay_context: When Met30 separates from its usual partner Skp1, such as during cadmium exposure, it is still broken down by a different degradation system that does not need Skp1 but uses the cell's protein recycling machinery.
allowed_evidence_spans: Cadmium exposure leads to dissociation of Met30 from Skp1 thereby generating a burst of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30, which needs to be controlled by the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway.

We were interested in how cells cope with the generated excess of Met30 because the well-described autocatalytic F-box protein degradation pathway mechanism cannot act on Met30 during these conditions . Interestingly , degradation of the F-box protein Met30 was maintained and even slightly induced in response to cadmium stress .

A mutant form of Met30 lacking its entire F-box domain ( Met30ΔFbox ) was constitutively unstable even though cells did not experience cadmium stress . Rapid degradation of Met30ΔFbox was observed both in cycloheximide chase and promoter shut-off experiments , indicating that components of this degradation pathway are constitutively present and that new protein synthesis is not required .

Collectively these results demonstrate that disruption of the Met30-Skp1 interaction , by either active signal-induced dissociation ( cadmium stress ) or by mutations in Met30 or Skp1 , induces rapid degradation of the F-box protein Met30 .
forbidden_overgeneralizations: all F-box proteins degraded this way

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The Skp1-independent degradation pathway requires the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but not Skp1, showing a novel function of Cdc53.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: An additional degradation pathway for Met30 dissociated from Skp1 requires Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of Skp1, with Cdc53 able to bind Met30 directly and mediate its degradation.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This pathway requires part of the SCF core but not Skp1.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The protein Cdc53, part of the SCF complex, can promote degradation of Met30 even when Skp1 is not present, revealing a new role for Cdc53 separate from its usual partner.
allowed_evidence_spans: Here we describe an additional pathway for regulation of F-box proteins on the example of yeast Met30 . This ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1 . Unexpectedly , this pathway required the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but was independent of the other central SCF component Skp1 .

Together these results suggest existence of a novel mechanism of Met30 regulation that specifically targets Met30 that is displaced from Skp1 and is dependent on the ubiquitin proteasome system and requires the function of Cdc53 , Rbx1 and Cdc34 , but not Skp1 .
The experiments with skp1 single and skp1 cdc53 double mutants strongly suggested that the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway for Met30 was dependent on Cdc53 and independent of Skp1

Not only was Met30 degradation active in the absence of Skp1 in vivo, but in addition a Cdc53 mutant incapable of binding to Skp1 could fully complement the Met30 degradation defect of cdc53 mutants. In addition, Cdc53/Rbx1 can directly bind Met30 in the absence of Skp1 in vitro and binding depends on the degron region adjacent to the F-box motif.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The Skp1-independent, Cul1-dependent degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and defense against heavy metal stress.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: This non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress in yeast.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This pathway is important for cell health under stress.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The alternative degradation system that works without Skp1 helps yeast cells keep their chromosomes stable and survive harmful heavy metal exposure.
allowed_evidence_spans: We demonstrated that this non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress .
Cells expressing Met30M178E/I179E were significantly more sensitive and exhibited a growth arrest in response to cadmium stress.
In addition to enhanced cadmium sensitivity, Met30M178E/I179E mutants displayed increased chromosome loss.

evidence_rows.abstract_claim: The SCF core components Cdc53, Rbx1, and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 mediate Skp1-independent ubiquitylation and degradation of unbound Met30, revealing additional diversity in cullin-RING ligases.
evidence_rows.core_keep_af: The SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1, along with the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34, are involved in the Skp1-independent ubiquitylation and degradation of unbound Met30, suggesting a novel function of Cdc53/Cul1.
evidence_rows.expert_summary_hint: This adds an additional layer to understanding E3 ligase regulation.
evidence_rows.lay_context: The study shows that parts of the SCF complex, including Cdc53, Rbx1, and Cdc34, can tag Met30 for destruction even without Skp1, indicating more complexity in how these protein complexes work.
allowed_evidence_spans: This degradation pathway targets Met30 that is detached from Skp1 and involves the SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1 , as well as the cognate SCF ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 . Importantly , this ubiquitylation pathway does not require Skp1 ( Skp1-independent Cul1-dependent ubiquitylation ) and suggests a function of Cdc53/Cul1 that is independent from association with Skp1 .
Met30 can interact with Cdc53/Rbx1 in vitro at a site distinct from the Skp1 binding domain of Cdc53.
Together, our findings shed light on the regulation and complexity of E3 ligases and suggest additional diversity in the cullin-RING family of ubiquitin ligases.
forbidden_overgeneralizations: all cullin-RING ligases have this function
